lines: The app ships no composer/autoload.php, so the server registers its generic loader for lib/ and looks every class up in the file system.

A composer/composer.json with config.vendor-dir ".", config.optimize-autoloader true, a config.autoloader-suffix and autoload.psr-4 {"OCA\\LDAPContactsBackend\\": "../lib/"} makes composer dump-autoload write composer/autoload.php with a class map; the code of the app does not change.
vendor/ ships 1 package that the server ships itself in a major of Nextcloud 34. Both copies define the same classes, and the autoloader that is asked first decides which version runs.
7 uses of the private API of the server in 7 files. Only OCP and NCU are public: what is below OC changes without notice between majors.

boot() registers a listener or takes a service from the container in 1 place. boot() runs once for every process of the server, so each of them is built on every request. registerEventListener() in register() builds a listener only when its event fires.

places: lib/Controller/ContactsController.php:58 OCP\Constants::PERMISSION_CREATE: deprecated since Nextcloud 13; Use \OCP\Constants::PERMISSION_CREATE instead

lines: 2 uses in 2 files of the public API that is deprecated in Nextcloud 34. The text of the tag names the replacement where it has one.
lib/Controller/ContactsController.php:58 OCP\Constants::PERMISSION_CREATE: deprecated since Nextcloud 13; Use \OCP\Constants::PERMISSION_CREATE instead
lib/Service/ContactsAddressBook.php:102 OCP\Constants::PERMISSION_READ: deprecated since Nextcloud 13; Use \OCP\Constants::PERMISSION_READ instead

The app reads and writes its app config in 2 places and registers no config lexicon, which IRegistrationContext::registerConfigLexicon() takes since Nextcloud 31. A lexicon states the type, the default and the sensitivity of each key in one place.
